title: Decompose capacity-planner and isolate node provisioning side effects
creator: Lena Park
description: Summary: The capacity planner and the GPU node lifecycle controller currently share responsibilities that create hard-to-reason side effects: provisioning retries trigger planner state churn, taint/toleration transitions are handled in multiple places, and cloud provider backoff logic is duplicated. This ticket decomposes the planner into a pure decision engine and a separate provisioning executor with explicit side-effect boundaries. Goals are to reduce flakiness during scale events, make unit testing feasible, and unlock a follow-up change to consolidate cloud SDKs and bump our Kubernetes client dependency.
acceptance_criteria: CapacityPlanner produces an immutable plan object describing required adjustments (scale up/down, drain, cordon) with no I/O side effects
ProvisioningExecutor consumes plan objects and performs cloud/provider operations; it has retries and backoff localized and logged clearly
Node lifecycle transitions (Provisioning -> Ready -> Draining -> Terminated) are orchestrated through a single state-machine module with a defined interface consumed by both controllers
E2E test suite covers a simulated rapid scale-up and scale-down without transient duplicate provisioning attempts (stable counts within SLAs)
Observability: planner emits plan diffs and executor emits action events; existing dashboards updated to show plan vs. actual reconciliation timelines
Benchmark: median reconciliation latency reduced by at least 20% in the synthetic load test compared to baseline run 2025-01-28
technical_notes: Split capacity-planner package into planner core (deterministic algorithms) and planner-api (plan serialization and validation).
Introduce ProvisioningExecutor interface: Execute(plan) -> ExecutionReport. Executor will own cloud SDK retries, lease acquisition, and node tagging operations.
Refactor node lifecycle to a single state-machine module under node-controller/pkg/lifecycle with events and guards; existing inline state transitions will be migrated incrementally.
Replace ad-hoc backoff code with a shared backoff util (exponential with jitter) and add metrics for backoff occurrences to aid debugging.
Keep public RPC/HTTP APIs unchanged; adapter layers will translate current calls into planner requests to avoid breaking other teams during rollout.
Plan for Kubernetes client-go upgrade in a follow-up PR after interfaces stabilize (this ticket avoids mixing upgrade with behavior changes to simplify rollback).
Add thorough unit tests for planner core using deterministic random seeds for placement heuristics to make CI reproducible.
migration_plan: 1) Land planner-core and planner-api refactor behind feature flag 'planner_v2' with no default activation
2) Deploy ProvisioningExecutor skeleton that logs actions but performs no mutations (dry-run mode) for one week; monitor plan vs action divergence
3) Flip planner_v2 for a small subset of GPU pools (canary) and run dry-run executor; collect metrics and fix issues
4) Enable executor mutation for canary pools during low-traffic window, observe, then progressively increase rollout
5) Once stable, remove feature flag and deprecate old planner endpoints; schedule client-go upgrade ticket as separate change
Rollback: restore previous planner adapter and stop executor mutator; executor dry-run state is harmless and can be reinstated quickly
risks: Risk: mis-synchronization window between planner decision and executor mutation could cause temporary overprovisioning. Mitigation: add lock/lease per-pool and idempotency keys on executor actions.
Risk: increased logging and new metrics could exceed ingestion quotas. Mitigation: rate-limit plan diffs and use sampling for high-frequency events.
Risk: edge-case of spot/interruptible instances handling differs across clouds. Mitigation: executor will have cloud-specific strategy modules and integration tests per provider.
Risk: rollout may surface latent bugs in taint handling. Mitigation: extended canary and a health gate requiring zero taint-mismatch alerts for 24h
